explanation: This pole fires on the tokens of a text that are not whole, frequent Latin-script words: word-interior pieces of multi-piece words and identifiers ('in' in 'veterinarian', 'used' in 'perused', 'ith' in 'ornithologist', ' diss', 'ind'), non-Latin-script characters (nearly all of them, most tokens 0.10-0.14 with the peak at the 0.17 ceiling), numerals, and whole words outside the most frequent English vocabulary; it also fires on a text's opening tokens, where the layer-2 residual has no context yet. It is exactly zero on running prose built only from the most frequent whole words and common punctuation ('the', 'of', 'and', 'was', 'read', 'book', ',', '.'), so 'The students read the book and then they wrote the exercises.' peaks at 0.000 while 'Students read books and then they wrote exercises in class that day.' peaks at 0.167.
